intended_object: Take a morphism φ : S₁ → S₂ between sequences of n composable arrows that are both complexes. For indices i, j = i+1, k = j+1 ≤ n, φ induces a morphism between the short complexes S₁(i) → S₁(j) → S₁(k) and S₂(i) → S₂(j) → S₂(k). The definition is meant to be this morphism, as the docstring ("functoriality maps for sc'") says.
explanation:
The definition builds a morphism of short complexes. Its three components are the components of the natural transformation φ at the positions i, j and k. It states no commutativity conditions explicitly; those (`comm₁₂`, `comm₂₃`) are left to the structure's auto-param defaults, which follow from the naturality of φ. This is exactly the induced map, so the definition is correct.

It is also at its natural generality. It only needs a category with zero morphisms, which is already required for short complexes to make sense. It works for any length n and any pair of composable-arrow sequences that are complexes. Mathlib has no other declaration of this specific induced map; the definition itself is the Mathlib declaration (in `Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/ExactSequence.lean`), so the counterpart field is left empty.
